problem: An empty signature always verifies. expected[:0] is '' and compare_digest('', '') returns True, so every payload passes.
failure: verify(b'{"user":"admin"}', '') returns True without knowledge of KEY, which bypasses authentication completely.
fix: Accept only fixed signature lengths, such as len(sig) in {V1_SIG_LEN, 64}, and reject any other length before comparing.

problem: There is no minimum signature length, so the client decides how strong the check is. A prefix of 1 to 4 hex characters can be brute-forced.
failure: Try sig values '0' through 'f' with any forged payload. One of the 16 attempts returns True, and a 4-character prefix takes at most 65,536 attempts.
fix: Require a fixed v1 length constant and the full 64-character length, and reject every other length.

problem: The truncation applies to every caller, not only v1 clients. Nothing links the short form to a protocol version, so full-length (v2) verification can be silently downgraded.
failure: A v2 endpoint that expects 64-character HMACs still accepts an attacker's truncated signature, because verify() is never told the caller's version. Every token is then only as strong as the length the attacker sends.
fix: Move v1 compatibility into an explicit path with a fixed length, such as verify_v1 or a version parameter, and keep full-length comparison as the default.
